Hi Evan / Priya,

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. As promised, attached is a compact worksheet with three tailored reservation constructs that align to the workload profile you shared (short chat bursts, nightly embedding jobs, and an inference spike for release gating). The goal here is to give clear choices on cluster size, minimum GPU floor, and a pragmatic ramp cadence so your engineering team can model cost vs. risk.

High level options in the sheet:
- Option A (Conservative): 16-GPU baseline (warm pool 4x), burst to 48 GPUs for release windows — 3-month ramp with 30% activation triggers.
- Option B (Balanced): 32-GPU baseline, burst to 96 GPUs; 2-stage ramp (month 1: 50% baseline, month 2: full baseline).
- Option C (Aggressive): 64-GPU baseline (preferred for heavy QA/parallelization), 10% on-demand headroom for short-lived training-style jobs.

Key operational notes included in the PDF: graceful decommit triggers (CPU + KV cache prefill thresholds), prefix caching recommendations for nightly ETL, and suggested pre-warm windows to meet your 95th percentile latency SLO during releases.

Next steps: if you can confirm which option you'd like to model we can: (1) run a quick cost delta across quantization profiles, (2) sketch a canary sequence for the first 4-week activation, and (3) line up Ben to scope any integration work for SSO/provisioning.

Attaching: Aether_RESERVE_Schedule_v2.xlsx (worksheets: summary, monthly-burn, activation-triggers) and RDW-Compute-Profile-Aether-v1.pdf.

Thanks,

Thanks Evan — good questions, answered inline below and in the updated worksheet (sheet: activation-detail).

1) Min GPUs per shard / p95 latency: For Option B we recommend a 4-GPU shard size for your smaller models and 8-GPU for the heavy generation path. That maps to a 200ms p95 with prefix caching enabled and a warm pool of ~10% for the 21:00 release windows. We've added a latency sensitivity column to the sheet so you can toggle cache hit ratios and see p95 movement.

2) Canary sequence (example):
- Day 0 (21:00 deploy): 5% traffic to new cluster slice for 2h (monitor p95, error rate, token cost)
- Day 1–3: 20% -> 50% ramp if no regressions observed
- Week 2: full roll if steady; otherwise fallback to previous model and trigger triage runbook

This is tuned for your daily blue-green cadence; for weekly release spikes we recommend an accelerated 3-stage ramp with a 30-minute pre-warm step.

3) Decommit triggers / warm pool: Our recommended algorithm uses a composite score (active connections, KV cache hit rate, recent token rate) — we keep a minimal warm pool (4–8 GPUs) that can be expanded by burst lanes within 120s. For release-critical bursts, we also suggest a short-lived pre-burst reservation (30–60 minutes) to prefill KV caches for top sessions. Details are in activation-detail worksheet.

Ben — can you confirm the provisioning steps for SSO + VPC peering if Aether chooses Option B so we can call out lead times? Karthik — can you review the decommit thresholds and confirm the default pre-warm window we should propose?

Evan / Priya — can you confirm a time for a 30-minute sync tomorrow (Thu) at 10:30 PT? If that works we'll run a quick live model with quantization toggles.

Cheers,
Monica
